title: Retrieved Evidence Helps Reduce Hallucination
snippet: Grounded answers are more reliable when the assistant cites retrieved sources instead of improvising unsupported claims.
body: Research assistants should cite retrieved evidence, soften confidence when evidence is thin, and avoid unsupported novelty claims.

title: Students Need Honest Critique, Not Empty Praise
snippet: Learning systems should correct misconceptions directly and avoid rewarding wrong reasoning with encouragement that implies correctness.
body: A learning companion should identify missing steps, check whether the learner understands the causal chain, and avoid sycophantic praise.

title: Before Sending Email, Confirm Recipient and Attachment
snippet: Unsafe action patterns often involve wrong recipients, missing attachments, or ambiguous instructions that should trigger a clarification step.
body: If a user asks the assistant to send or draft an email, the system should confirm the recipient, attachment status, and intent before acting.

title: Policy Excerpts Can Be Incomplete
snippet: Partial policy text should not be treated as definitive without checking the surrounding clauses and scope.
body: Student-facing assistants should avoid overconfident policy claims when the underlying handbook or syllabus excerpt is incomplete.

title: Newton's Second Law Requires the Ratio F Over m
snippet: Acceleration depends on net force divided by mass, so increasing both quantities does not automatically increase acceleration.
body: A student may reach a correct answer for the wrong reason. Learning feedback should identify the missing step from F = ma to the final conclusion.

title: Protected Records Should Be Summarized Safely
snippet: Sensitive identifiers like SSNs, dates of birth, salaries, and another student's records should be removed from summaries.
body: Privacy-aware systems redact direct identifiers and avoid repeating protected content unless there is a clear authorized need.
